Subject: Post-demo: summary + next steps on SOC 2 / HIPAA / questionnaire

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your procurement and security teams have what they need: 

What we covered (high-level)
- Redwood hosted and Private options for inference (Hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private VPC/on-prem).
- Data residency options (EU/US), ability to isolate PHI on Dedicated/Private.
- Compliance posture: SOC 2 Type II (production inference in-scope), GDPR support, roadmap for ISO/FedRAMP.

Action items I committed to:
1) Share a redacted copy of our most recent SOC 2 Type II report and a privacy datasheet — attached.
2) Kick off your vendor security questionnaire (I see you shared a copy during the call) — we will return a completed draft by Wed 30 Jun.
3) Confirm BAAs and HIPAA support: short answer — we support HIPAA workloads on Dedicated and Private deployments and can sign a BAA; I’ll loop in our security lead for details.
4) Provide a recommended scope for SOC expansion and an ISO27001 timeline so you can align procurement expectations.

Questions we need from you (to prioritize):
- Will MediWell process PHI in production with Redwood (yes/no)?
- Any strict EU-only residency requirement or can we propose a US region with contract clauses?
- Procurement timeline and target go-live date?

Attachments: redwood_SOC2_TypeII_redacted_2025.pdf, redwood_privacy_datasheet.pdf

Proposed next meeting: 30-minute security sync w/ your security, our security lead (vivek), and one of our SEs (grace). I’m available Tue 30 Jun 10-11am PT or Wed 30 Jun 2-4pm PT — what works?

Thanks —
Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the recap, this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) PHI: yes, MediWell will process PHI in production for our care coordination workflows. We need explicit confirmation that PHI can be kept in a dedicated environment and that you will sign a BAA for that deployment.
2) HIPAA attestation / BAA: our legal team requires a copy of your BAA template and any details on subcontractor access. Can your security team confirm whether Redwood uses any third-party logging/analytics that might capture content?
3) GDPR / Residency: we have one EU data residency requirement for a pilot site — ideally EU-hosted inference. If Private VPC isn’t feasible for the pilot, we need contractual guarantees for EU-only processing.
4) Procurement timeline: target pilot start = 2026-08-15. Procurement will need completed security questionnaire and SOC 2 by 2026-07-07 to keep that timeline.

Attached is our vendor questionnaire (MediWell_Security_Q_2026.xlsx). Please let me know who on your team will own returning answers and timelines for each section.

I can do the security sync Tue 30 Jun at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Emma Hayes

From: grace oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: MediWell questionnaire + next steps (ownership)

Thanks — quick update and planned deliverables before Wed 1 Jul EOD.

1) HIPAA & BAA: We support HIPAA-covered workloads on Dedicated and Private deployment models. For Hosted (multi-tenant) we do not recommend PHI. We do have a standard BAA template that our legal team can sign for Dedicated/Private. I attached the standard BAA excerpt and key subcontractor list in the worksheet we’ll return.

2) SOC 2: Our SOC 2 Type II (period ending 2025) covers production inference and supporting infra. I’m attaching a redacted copy (redwood_SOC2_TypeII_redacted_2025.pdf). Vivek will add a one-page SOC scope summary callout for their procurement packet.

3) Questionnaire: I started filling the technical tabs in MediWell_Security_Q_2026.xlsx and attached our working answers (redwood_vendor_q_answers_2026-06.xlsx). Highlights:
- Encryption at rest & in transit: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+/TLS1.3 in transit. Customer-managed keys via KMS supported on Dedicated/Private; HSM integrations possible for Private.
- Data residency: We can provision inference nodes in EU regions for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we offer EU regions but data replication across regions happens only with explicit config/contract.
- Access controls & logging: Role-based access, token-level audit logs, and optional log forwarding to customer SIEM. We redact model I/O in logs by default for privacy-sensitive workloads.

4) ISO / FedRAMP: ISO27001 adoption is in our roadmap; formal program start date is targeted Q4 2026 with certification goal in 2027. FedRAMP is a longer path (multi-year); we can discuss interim compensating controls for government customers but do not currently hold FedRAMP authorization.

Attachments: redwood_vendor_q_answers_2026-06.xlsx, redwood_SOC2_TypeII_redacted_2025.pdf

I’ll be on the security sync Tue 30 Jun 10am PT with Jonas and Emma. Vivek — could you please prepare the SOC scope one-pager and a short note on third-party subprocessors?

—Grace
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
